title: prompt-drafts-and-prompt-library-experiments
content:
Purpose / notes
- Personal scratchpad for prompt templates + few-shot sets I'm iterating on for the embeddings + chat endpoint experiments.
- Keep rough failure cases, prompt footprints (token counts), and quick heuristics for when to switch model variants (gpt-like vs. instruction-tuned open models).
- Not a final library; intermediate experiments and ideas to later move into repo under samples/prompt-library.

Current goals
1) Build compact few-shot templates for customer support summarization that are robust to hallucination.
2) Create a short heuristic checklist (2–3 rules) for when to use Rerank vs. direct generation.
3) Collect representative failure cases (3 per template) to use for regression tests / evals.

Notes on format decisions
- Template pieces: system instruction (one short sentence), 0–5 shots (each: user+assistant), then user prompt.
- Try to keep final prompt < 3.5k tokens for latency budget on Dedicated small slices. For long contexts use embeddings + retrieve+condense.
- Use explicit "If you don't know, say 'I don't know'" phrasing to reduce confident hallucinations. Works often but not perfect.

Template A: Support-summary-short (for chat endpoint)
- System: "You are a helpful customer support assistant. Produce a concise, unbiased summary and list of action items."
- Shots: 2 short examples (see below)
- User: "Conversation: <conversation_text>
Please produce: 1) one-paragraph summary (3-4 lines), 2) bullet action items with owner if mentioned, 3) list of open questions the user asked."

Example shots (few-shot)
1) User: "Customer: My app crashes on login after I update. I see error 502, restarting doesn't help. I'm on iPhone 12, iOS 17.0.2."
   Assistant: "Summary: Customer reports crash on login after update, error 502 on iPhone 12 (iOS 17.0.2). Action items: - engineering: investigate 502 during auth flow; - support: ask for device logs. Open questions: Has the customer tried clearing app cache?"
2) User: "Customer: The invoice total is wrong; tax calculated twice. Occurred on web checkout 2024-12-03."
   Assistant: "Summary: Customer reports duplicate tax on invoice during web checkout (2024-12-03). Action items: - billing: verify tax calc rules; - support: request invoice #. Open questions: Was a promo code applied?"

Notes on failure cases we've seen
- Long conversations (10+ turns) -> model drops earlier details: mitigation: run a short retrieval step to highlight top-3 user complaints then feed into summary template.
- Ambiguous owner mentions: "Will CC John" -> model arbitrarily assigns owner. Mitigation: only list explicit owner names; otherwise mark as "unassigned".
- Multiple issues in a single thread -> model mixes action items. Mitigation: ask assistant to enumerate issues separately (explicit numbered list).

Template B: Short Rerank prompt (for embedding-rerank flow)
- Purpose: Given top-20 candidate answers from retrieval, rerank to top-3 by relevance + factuality.
- Prompt format: system: "You are a strict relevance and factuality judge. Rank candidate answers based on how well they answer the query, penalize hallucinated facts."
- Shots: 1 example where a plausible-sounding but incorrect answer is ranked below a shorter precise factual answer.

Rerank heuristics
- Prefer answers that cite explicit evidence from snippet (if provided).
- Penalize answers with invented dates/names not present in sources.
- If multiple answers tie, prefer shorter answer (concise precision).

Failure cases observed
- Model still prefers fluent hallucination when snippet is noisy. Try: include a small instruction to "only use facts present in the candidate snippets; if none, return 'insufficient info'".
- Token-cost: rerank prompt + all candidates can blow token budget. Optimize by compressing candidates (strip fluff).

Experiment log (short)
- 2025-01-15: Ran support-summary-short with gpt-like open-1-8k (bench). F1 on action-item extraction: 0.62. Notes: hallucination reduced when adding explicit "If unsure say 'I don't know'".
- 2025-01-20: Rerank flow w/ embeddings-v2 + small-instr model as judge. RR@1 improved from 0.54 -> 0.69 but latency + cost increased 2.1x.

Prompt footprint / tokens (approx)
- support-summary-short: system 12 tokens, 2 shots ~220 tokens, user prompt + conversation variable (avg 700 tokens) -> template baseline ~932 tokens.
- rerank prompt: system 18 tokens, candidates compressed -> ~1200 tokens total for 20 candidates (too big). Aim to keep < 1k.

Open action items (TODO)
- [ ] Convert top-3 templates to canonical JSON spec for samples repo (fields: system, shots[], prompt, expected_output_schema).
- [ ] Add regression tests: 5 failure threads per template with expected outputs + tolerances. (Linear INF-321)
- [ ] Run batch eval on Dedicated small slice to measure latency impact at QPS=5. (assign to Liam?)

Quick heuristics for model selection (notes)
- Use instruction-tuned smaller model for rerank/judging (low-cost, tolerant to short context).
- Use larger context open model for summarization of long threads only if embeddings-retrieval isn't sufficient.
- If output requires up-to-date facts (dates, versions) prefer retrieval + explicit citation.

Links and references
- Linear ticket: INF-321 (prompt library + regression tests)
- GitHub PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/87 (initial skeleton)
- Confluence: /confluence/support-summaries (draft design doc)

Misc notes / quick experiments to try next
- Try chain-of-thought style instruction for rerank (ask judge to say why candidate is wrong). Check latency tradeoffs.
- Test explicit "format: JSON" outputs for action items so downstream parsers are deterministic. But watch for hallucinated keys vs. text outputs.
- Test few-shot with negative examples (one shot showing a hallucination and correct judge response) to teach model to penalize hallucination.

Draft failure-case bank (short examples)
1) Multi-issue thread: customer reports login + invoice problems in same thread -> expected behavior: produce two separate issue summaries and action items.
2) Implicit owner: "Can you ask Alex?" -> expected: owner "Alex" only if Alex explicitly in thread; otherwise unassigned.
3) Fabricated date: user says "it happened in June" but model invents exact day -> expected: use only mentioned granularity.

Notes to self: keep this doc informal. When stable, move to samples/prompt-library as 'support-summary-v1' and create regression test harness.

End of scratchpad.
